reasons: Classification is correct: 11.1(c) creates joint ownership and 11.1(d) confines each Party to internal-purpose practice with no right to license, enforce or assign absent consent (save where the joint IP happens to sit inside the licences granted). That is 'joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit', which the rule expressly puts in walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback rather than merely falling short of the preferred wording.

Redline is directionally right and actionable: it restores an unrestricted right for each Party to practise, exploit and license co-owned IP 'subject only to the exclusive licenses expressly granted under this Agreement', so Ono's exclusive Product/Territory rights and Array's grant-back are preserved, and no assignment of our IP or data to the counterparty is introduced.

Edit is confined to the single offending sentence; the remaining Joint Patent prosecution/enforcement sentences are left intact, so the 0.741 changed-character ratio reflects a necessary sentence-level rewrite rather than an over-broad rewrite of the clause.

The retained consent gate on assigning a co-ownership interest (with Affiliate / permitted-assignment carve-outs) keeps the edit proportionate and does not disadvantage us; the rationale correctly records that the rest of the IP architecture (11.1(a), 2.6 grant-back, 4.7-4.8 data licences, 4.2(b)-(c), Article XII trademark assignment) is already acceptable, so there is no double-flagging.

Comment is accurate on what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and stays within tone; minor point only — the new sentence does not expressly restore enforcement rights, which remain governed by the surviving consult/mutual-agreement language, so consider adding 'enforce' for internal consistency.
